newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL rubber ends up on Tokyo gain despite Thai news.
newsitem.headline: KL rubber ends up on Tokyo gain despite Thai news.

text.p: The Malaysian rubber market ended higher with local dealers covering, and on gains in Tokyo. News that Thailand will not accept rubber bought from the market to cut losses had no immediate impact, traders said.
"The market did not react immediately to the Thailand news because of higher Tokyo values and the ringgit's weakness against the dollar," a dealer at a trading firm said.
"The market was a bit confused and prices would definitely come off in the near term. The exporters who sold the rubber to the government have to resell to somebody in the market," the dealer added.
"It will have an impact on the prices soon because it is not one or two tonnes but... 23,100 tonnes," another dealer said.
"Rubber will be freely offered in the market and the price of the commodity will just tumble," he said.

Thailand Deputy Prime Minister Sukhawich Rangsitphol announced late on Thursday that Bangkok will not take delivery of the rubber to trim losses, as part of an official scheme to prop up domestic rubber prices.
However some dealers said a weaker Malaysian ringgit against the U.S. dollar could limit any sharp falls.
